headline: Cemetery growth offsets funeral margin pressure
summary_short: Revenue rose 3.6% y/y to $1,103.3 million on a 5.1% jump in comparable cemetery revenue, but diluted EPS of $0.90 was down 7.2% sequentially as higher preneed-driven selling compensation compressed funeral gross margin to 18.5% from 19.8% a year ago.
summary_long: Cemetery strength (comparable revenue +4.8%, gross profit +5.0% on 8.0% preneed sales growth) more than offset a 4.9% funeral gross-profit decline, as preneed-driven selling compensation rose while a 3.3% gain in comparable average revenue per service ($6,016) couldn't fully offset a 1.4% dip in services performed. Corporate G&A fell to $41.8M (from $49.5M, which included a $6.4M legal settlement). Diluted EPS was $0.90, up 4.7% y/y on lower share count but down 7.2% q/q. Current debt maturities jumped to $195.1M from $56.8M as $136.9M of 2027 notes moved inside 12 months. FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance confirmed at a $4.20 midpoint (narrowed to $4.10-$4.30); operating cash flow guidance raised to a $1,085M midpoint (+$50M) on stronger cemetery preneed receipts.

drivers.explanation: Company frames the y/y increase as driven by higher cemetery gross profit, lower corporate G&A, and a lower share count, partly offset by lower funeral gross profit from higher selling compensation on preneed production.
Funeral revenue +$13.4M (acquisitions/new construction +$9.4M, comparable +$5.1M); cemetery revenue +$24.4M (comparable preneed revenue +$22.8M, new/acquired properties +$1.6M).

Funeral gross profit fell $5.7M (-4.9%) on higher selling compensation tied to strong insurance-funded preneed production; cemetery gross profit rose $7.7M (+5.0%) on higher preneed volume, largely offsetting.
Y/y increase attributed to higher cemetery gross profit, lower corporate G&A ($41.8M vs $49.5M, which included a $6.4M prior-year legal settlement charge), and a lower share count.

Current maturities of long-term debt rose to $195.1M from $56.8M at 2025 year-end as the $136.9M 7.500% Senior Notes due April 2027 moved within 12 months and were reclassified from long-term to current.
Grew q/q despite the ~$136.9M reclass of the 2027 notes to current, consistent with the company's disclosed ~$189M rise in average floating-rate debt balances funding buybacks and capex.
Reflects share repurchases: 3.35 million shares bought back in H1 2026 for $264.9 million (avg $79.04/share), cutting the diluted share count y/y.
Rose y/y to $0.90 from $0.86 on net income growth plus a lower diluted share count from buybacks; fell q/q against Q1's stronger comparable trends.
